explanation: Fires on speech/attribution verbs, mostly 'say/said/says' (and sometimes 'told me'), right after the subject that introduces a reported statement or opinion (e.g. 'Payton said', 'we can say', 'critics say'). Other cognition/reporting verbs that introduce a clause ('found', 'mean', 'announcing', 'telling') get moderate activation; desire/plan verbs ('want', 'hope', 'plans') only weak.

No clear shared concept: fires on mid-word subword pieces of foreign or unusual names (Khuras-an, Sch-les-wig, Stojanovi-ć, Ph-usion, Tsur-ugi), on garbled multibyte characters, and also on function words in phrases like 'some [of]', 'as well [as]', 'goal is [to]'. Seems a mixture of word-fragment continuation and quantity/partitive constructions.

Fires on many unrelated tokens: mid-word fragments of rare or compound words (rhin-oc-eros, hermaphro-dit-ism, sum-pt-uous, mid-wife, break-water, Sh-and-ong) and also function words heading relative/prepositional phrases ('the place [where]', 'parents [who]', 'use [which] roads', '[while] driving', 'family [for] years'). No single predictable rule.

Mixture: strongest on biomedical subword starts like 'gluc'(ocorticoid/osyl), 'micro[s]urgical/omal', 'Vit'rectomy, plus the number word 'one' in 'nearly one million / one-third / one of'; also fires on unrelated code tokens ('<form', '.Math', '_s', '=') and name fragments. No coherent single trigger.

Strongest on the piece 'iff' in names like Giffard/Giffords (and 'if' in aquifolium); otherwise fires moderately on a scatter of tokens, largely in non-English (French, Portuguese, Spanish) text and inside names or abbreviations (Bokova, Lanzini, FSH, nebivolol). Apart from the 'iff' fragment, hard to predict.

Mostly fires on structural/boilerplate tokens in code and markup: line-initial 'import' after a block of Java imports, indentation before XML/Android attributes, separators in copyright year lists ('2016, 2018[,]'), package-path pieces ('.h'), tag closers. Also scattered hits in prose (date-range dash in career lists, 'nada menos [que]'). Loosely 'repetitive structured-list continuation' but noisy.

Fires inside questions and embedded wh-/how-clauses, on the token right after the question word or modal: 'how [to] prevent', 'how does [Leia] know', 'What['s]', 'would [it] lead', 'Could this be [the]', 'know [who]', and on the start of an answer ('A: [You] can'). Scattered other hits (word fragments like engra-ft, SPARQL '?title').

Fires on the main verb (or the word right after it) that comes after a long subject noun phrase, i.e. where the predicate begins following a heavy subject: '...complex diseases [has]', '...a component [is] provided', 'studies regarding ... [are] lacking', 'turned [out]', 'purpose [of]'. Also fires on the first word of a new sentence in German/Norwegian ('Jeg', 'Wer'). Short subjects give little activation.

Fires on soil, compost and nutrient-cycling vocabulary: humus, compost, humic, peat, soil, fertilizer, poultry litter, sludge, nitrogen/phosphate, nutrient cycling. Strongest in gardening/soil contexts; unrelated tokens barely activate.

Diffuse: fires on many content words (often verbs or adjectives) in mid-sentence predicate positions ('fulfilling', 'closed', 'raises', 'rings hollow', 'opens', 'fill', 'create') and also on code/CSS tokens ('padding', 'Elastic', 'TearDown', '"License"'). No clear shared feature.

Fires mostly on separators and function words in technical, code or non-English (Portuguese/French) text: 'https[://]', version-number dots, hyphens in 'caspase-2' and '2019-2020', LaTeX backslash, '="' in attributes, 'from __future__ [import]', and Portuguese/French auxiliaries ('estar', 'été', 'pela'). A loose mixture.

Fires on verbs of transferring possession or information to someone else: share, pass (on), give (up), sell, send, rent out, yield control, deed property, lend, turn over, plus the particle/object right after such a verb ('pass [the] virus', 'pass this data [on]'). Weaker on related transfer words (traded, transferred, brought into).

Two main triggers: 'to' in 'happen(s/ed) to be/to' (coincidence construction), and '-sectional' in 'cross-sectional study'. Also scattered weaker hits ('can see', 'page load', name fragment 'Trenchard').

Fires on subword pieces inside South Asian (mainly Indian, also Bangladeshi/Pakistani) personal and place names, e.g. Anshul, Babul, Pramod, Pranav, Bhardwaj, Minakshi, Kanyakumari, Atal Bihari. Fires more when the context is clearly Indian; non-name tokens barely fire.

Fires at maximum on 'by' in the email header 'Forwarded by <name>' (and the '-----Original Message' marker); otherwise fires on a scatter of unrelated tokens (word fragments like retin-oid, plasmin-ogen, math-problem tokens, 'bill', 'tickets'). Apart from the email forward marker, unpredictable.

Fires weakly to moderately on fragments of proper names and identifiers (PACAP, StrCpy, Papio, Analytica, Chabot, Khachanov), on 'A' in 'A:' answer headers, and on 'defined' in C preprocessor lines. No consistent theme apart from the one strong 'PAC[AP]' example.

Fires on the opening parenthesis ' (' placed after a multi-word technical term to introduce its acronym (e.g. 'genome-wide association study (GWAS)', 'red blood cells (RBC)'), and on slashes joining alternatives ('languages/environments', 'She/He', 'local areas / companies'). Coordinators 'and/or' in lists give weaker activation.

Fires on tokens that open a nested block in code or markup, usually followed by a newline and indented content: '{' after a namespace/try, '(' after dashboardBody, XML container tags ending '>\n' (<appenders>, <elements>), JSON keys followed by ':' or '[' ('series:', 'hits":'). Prose hits are weak.

Strongest on ')' closing a newswire dateline credit '(AP)' or '(Reuters)' at the start of an article; also fires fairly strongly on assorted other tokens such as 'will' in future statements, 'Collect the terms [in]' in math problems, 'Glad [to]', 'Code [Generator]'. The dateline is the clearest part; the rest is a mixture.

Diffuse: fires on word-final suffix pieces (Anklev-ich, incident-ally, possibil-idades, there-from, analog-ues) and on function words in fixed phrases ('evidenced [by]', 'the fact [that]', 'unaware [of]', 'page [of]'), plus code tokens like '()' and '("'. No single predictable concept.

A mixture: fires on legal/licence boilerplate words (hereby, TORT, 'in the [hope]', 'intent to distribute', remanded), on PHP '->prepare', regex '(?<=', DOCTYPE '//', and assorted idiom pieces ('all the [rage]', 'what [sort] of', 'looks [like]'). No unifying rule.
